_note: SL-113, obligation O-018 (review M3): the class 'a figure worded at least that is not the store's lower bound'. Its members come from ordinary input: whoever wires the next surface (this slice's tree and list, then Q-292's follow-up that shows the listed figure beside the bound) passes the number they have in hand, and a rolled or listing figure sits ABOVE the final one (SL-112: 64 MiB shown against 1 MiB final), so the word in front of it is false on screen. The class is bounded by who produces its members: the values a caller can hold (arguments), the ways a bound is made (producers) and the places one is carried (carriers). Attempt 1 guarded it with a text rule over the spellings of one function's argument; legacy.rows shows what that rule did with each spelling, the 'before'. The design now closes it in the type system and AtLeastSeamTests holds the closure: no composer takes anything but the bound, the bound has no way in but the store's own read, and nothing else carries one. A new surface that needs a number worded as a bound adds a row here on purpose.

composers._note: Every non-private member of the App's text classes (compiled into Core.Tests as source) that has the at-least word in its name: each takes exactly one parameter, the bound. FolderTreeNode, which is only in the App assembly, calls these two and is held by the fitness rule 'the at-least word is composed only in TopLevelRowText' and by window case T-013's mutants.

producers._note: Callers, by the method they sit in (a lambda or a state machine is its method), found in the IL of every method of FsAnalyser.Core. The constructor is internal and Core grants InternalsVisibleTo to Core.Tests alone; a target-typed new(), var, a ternary or a local function all compile to the same newobj, which a text rule could not see.

carriers._note: Every field, property, method return and parameter of type AtLeastFigures or AtLeastFigures? in the assembly it is named in, other than the type's own members: a place a bound can sit or travel through.

legacy._note: Attempt 1's rule 'an at least figure is never the rolled or listing figure': its two patterns, run over one line of source each. fired is what they did when this corpus was written. A row that did not fire is a spelling the rule let through; each names the argument type (arguments above) it is, which the seam now refuses whatever it is spelled as. The rule was removed from .taad/fitness.yaml with this slice: it matched AtLeastSize(, which no longer exists, so it could never fire again.
